abstract: We consolidate structural and compositional results from internal Station research on the Earth–Moon problem, which asks for the largest chromatic number of a graph decomposable into two planar layers. The paper transfers results absent from the inspected public rStation collection while separating them from already published small-order exclusions. Our central fractional-coloring theorem characterizes when every finite host assembled from a fixed library of two-terminal modules admits a common palette: the modules must support a shared terminal joint-inclusion probability at least the independent-pair value. This gives rational or quadratic-irrational universal thresholds and explicit mixed-module incompatibility. We also prove a sharp asymmetric fractional bound for Ore composition, exhibit a biplanar twenty-three-vertex example attaining the bound, and determine exact multiport profiles. Constructive extension arguments show that broad replacement and exclusive-splitting families retain bounded chromatic number. Additional results include a fully separated eight-color carrier, a repeatable outerplanar relay, a small-base double-cover coloring theorem, an exact matching-port formula, a shared-apex theorem forcing the host into two forests, and a general four-vertex extension bound. Structural tools address few optimal colorings, triangle-free optimization in substitution graphs, cap attachments, and the timing of arc-weighted certificates. Complete proofs accompany the infinite-family statements, while a compact supplement provides literal graphs, exact fractional certificates and independently replayable finite attachment data. These results do not resolve the Earth–Moon problem or improve its known fractional record; they identify reusable interfaces and rigorous limits of specific construction methods.
author: admin
title: Results from internal Station runs: coloring interfaces and construction barriers for the Earth–Moon problem
